title: The Secret Service
author: Stuart, Dave
summary: Stuart reflects on the power and transformative nature of secret service—acts of kindness, help, and care given without recognition or expectation of return. In cultures obsessed with visibility, credit, and personal brand building, secret service is countercultural and profoundly transformative both for giver and receiver. Leaders who practice and encourage secret service build cultures of genuine generosity where people help others not for recognition or advancement but because it is right and needed. Secret service strengthens both the giver and receiver in ways visible service cannot.
points: Secret service—help given without recognition—is countercultural and deeply transformative.
Service for recognition shapes different culture than service without any expectation of return.
Secret service strengthens both giver and receiver in ways visible service cannot achieve.
Leaders who practice secret service build cultures of genuine generosity and care.
Encourage people to help others not for credit but because it is right.
The purest form of service is help given with absolutely no expectation of recognition.
Secret acts of kindness compound in culture in ways public recognition never will.
quotes: There is power in service that no one will ever know you gave.

True generosity is measured not by what you're given credit for, but by what you do in secret.
When you serve in secret, the impact is about the other person, not about you.
The most transformative leaders are often the least visible in their daily service to others.
Secret kindness has a way of multiplying in cultures that practice and value it.
Real culture change comes from leaders who model service without seeking recognition for it.” Archived from Substack (Dave Stuart) on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
